name: Intel Neural Compressor (multi-technique PTQ/QAT toolkit; low-bit LLM path is AutoRound)
bits: the toolkit spans INT8 / FP8 / MXFP8 / INT4 / MXFP4 / NVFP4 plus sparsity; its own advanced low-bit LLM/VLM quantization is DELEGATED to AutoRound
activation_scheme: static, dynamic, SmoothQuant-migrated outliers, or mixed precision - the technique is chosen per config, not fixed by the toolkit
kernels: FP8 static and dynamic quantization incl. Linear and FusedMoE on Gaudi
FP8 KV cache / Attention static quantization via AutoRound (experimental)
quality_delta: n/a - the README cites 'Faster Inference of LLMs using FP8 on the Intel Gaudi' (arXiv:2503.09975) but does not restate a delta inline. Null + note rather than paraphrasing a paper I did not read for this record.
notes: PROXY ENUM VALUE - DECLARED 2026-10-04: Intel Neural Compressor is a TOOLKIT spanning INT8 / FP8 / MXFP8 / INT4 / MXFP4 / NVFP4 plus sparsity and QAT - 'int8' names one member of a set that includes five-bit-exotic formats. The record's own kernels field makes the breadth explicit (MXFP8/MXFP4 and NVFP4 both marked experimental; FP8 static and dynamic incl. Linear and FusedMoE on Gaudi). Since its low-bit LLM path IS AutoRound, this record partly duplicates the autoround record. REQUESTED ENUM ADDITION: 'neural-compressor'. EXISTS AND IS BROAD, but the correct way to record it is as a TOOLKIT THAT DELEGATES rather than as a format. Techniques: Static Quantization, Dynamic Quantization, SmoothQuant, Weight-Only Quantization, Quantization-Aware Training, Mixed Precision. Frameworks: PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX (FP8 for Keras/JAX is new and experimental). Models: LLaMA, Qwen, DeepSeek, Flux and 10+ VLMs. THE KEY STRUCTURAL FACT: advanced low-bit LLM/VLM quantization (2-4 bit, MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8 KV cache) is not implemented in Neural Compressor - it is integrated FROM AutoRound, Intel's separate toolkit. So a practitioner asking 'what does Neural Compressor quantize to' should read the AutoRound scheme table instead (see the autoround record). Treating the two as one tool would misattribute the group_size and asymmetric-quantization restrictions. HARDWARE COVERAGE as stated by the project: Gaudi, Core Ultra, Xeon Scalable, Xeon CPU Max, Data Center GPU Flex and Data Center GPU Max are 'extensive'; AMD CPU, ARM CPU and NVIDIA GPU are 'limited testing'. Dated milestones from the README, useful for reading older docs: 2025-03 VLM quantization in a transformers-like API on Intel CPU/GPU; 2025-05 FP8 static quantization of DeepSeek V3/R1 on Gaudi; 2025-09 FP8 dynamic quantization including Linear and FusedMoE on Gaudi; 2025-10 MXFP8/MXFP4 (experimental); 2025-12 NVFP4 (experimental); 2026-03 FP8 for Keras/JAX and FP8 KV-cache/Attention static quantization via AutoRound (both experimental).
